scope: Bounded source-question draft for four current MC cards: dain II, daiin III, qodaiin III/open segmentation, and olkar hot/wood/share-I intersection. Source findings and untested decision contrasts remain separate.

questions.title: Shared value core versus surface-encoded axis and open qodaiin segmentation
questions.source_findings: GDT711 consolidates dain/daiin to abstract II/III cores and separates local grade/count realization. GDT686 independently states dain=d+II, daiin=d+III, qodaiin=qod+III, with visible quality versus substance/part heads selecting grade or quantity. It also records qod|aiin versus qo|daiin as unresolved boundaries and denies free qo credit.

models.core_axis: The whole-form core remains II/III; head/context selects quality or amount, and qodaiin remains a distinct III whole until segmentation is independently resolved.
models.surface_axis: The surface itself encodes a fixed grade or amount, so head-dependent alternation is only renderer context.
models.qod_segmentation: qod|aiin predicts affinity with qod forms; qo|daiin predicts affinity with daiin forms.

questions.different_observation: A source-bound set of repeated dain/daiin/qodaiin occurrences with independently typed quality-head versus part/measure-head contexts, plus a predeclared qodaiin neighbor comparison, would favor core-axis if the II/III contrast persists while axis changes with head; stable axis independent of head would favor surface-axis. A qodaiin comparison cannot be scored where no controlled neighbor frame exists.
questions.smallest_reopen: Use already admitted complete occurrences and preserve head/context labels; do not infer numeric units, quantity identity, or a qod component from German renderings.

questions.title: Olkar lexical intersection versus context-selected product referent
questions.source_findings: GDT711 retains only hot, wood, share I in the intersection of live olkar rivals and removes Ansatz/Auszug from the portable core. GDT693 retains six local Holz product contexts as Auszug rather than Ansatz, while explicitly treating this as a local referent change and not a second R meaning.

models.intersection_core: olkar has the bounded hot/wood/share-I core; preparation versus extract is selected by occurrence context and does not alter the lexical core.
models.lexical_context_split: olkar itself carries a stable preparation-versus-extract distinction that should recur independently of local apparatus/product context.

questions.different_observation: A predeclared matched set of olkar occurrences with independently observed preparation versus product cues would favor the intersection model if the same hot/wood/share-I core remains while the referent changes; a stable form-conditioned preparation/extract split under matched contexts would favor the rival. The six GDT693 examples are historical local evidence, not an independent confirmation.
questions.smallest_reopen: Keep Ansatz/Auszug as local rivals and require an independently scored cue for operation/product status; no free OL or OLK export.

evidence.quote:
V84 audits all 181 active W0/W1 readings and repairs the first 30 source readings (49 unchanged token positions on 25 pages). The central correction is architectural: the dictionary now stores a compact lexical core, while the occurrence table stores the practical local realization. Thus the seven active `daiin` senses collapse to one lexical core `Wert III`, with `Grad III` or `drei` retained only as context realizations; the three `dain` senses analogously collapse to `Wert II`.

The active dictionary contracts from 332 to 324 lexical readings without deleting or resegmenting any of the 479 token positions. The complete dictionary contracts from 1,594 to 1,586 readings while retaining 1,582 surfaces. Active levels are 11 W0, 149 W1, 145 W2 and 19 W3. Every historical confirmation remains `H0_NONE`, and GDT696–GDT709 still contribute zero word-confidence points.

## Material repairs

- Value family: `dain/daiin` become abstract values II/III; local grade-versus-count rendering is separate. `qodaiin` remains a distinct W1 `Wert III` reading; its decomposition field keeps `qod|aiin` versus `qo|daiin` open and QO receives no free semantic credit.
- Unsupported nouns and units are deleted: no automatic Gummi, Gran, Handvoll, Dosis, Mazerat, Absud or Auszug identity survives merely because a fluent renderer used it.
- `am/dam/dal/oidal` retain only visible measure/material structure; no historical unit is claimed.
- CKH forms retain exact-family `Mischgut/Mischung`, never a free universal CKH word or an identified medicine.
- `olkar` retains the intersection shared by both live rivals—hot, wood, share I—while Ansatz versus Auszug is removed. Free `ol` stays W1; bound `ol#2` stays W0 and nonportable.

## Guardrails

Exact normalized master-card matches are published as navigation links only and always receive automatic score credit 0. All 19 prior W3 readings and their 77 positions preserve meaning, score, semantic scope, applicability, export boundary, bound spans, writer and provenance. Structural readings remain structural; the compound-only `ol#2` is explicitly non-exportable. No new page, spelling, segmentation, historical analogue, plaintext identification, `f84`, or `f84r` is used.

evidence.role: olkar local rival and core/context policy
evidence.quote:
Six `olkar` contexts make a Holz product plausible through soaking, heating,
macerate context, subsequent additions or established amount binding. Their
apparatus reading is **Anteil I des heißen Holzauszugs** rather than **Anteil I
des heißen Holzansatzes**. They occur at f75r.3, f80r.17, f80v.35, f83v.12,
f86v3.13 and f86v6.5.

This is a change of local referent, not a second meaning for R. The selected
main therefore does not infer extraction wherever `olkar` occurs.

## Why Fraktion remains a serious runner-up

V65 used *Fraktion* in the technical sense “selected mixture share or material
class,” never as a claimed distillate. In that restricted sense it passes the
same morphological tests as *Anteil* and remains the closest rival.

It loses the main channel because ordinary modern German strongly invites a
separated-product reading. A near-period positive control illustrates the
difference: the late-fourteenth-/early-fifteenth-century
[*Anonimo Mediano*](https://corpus.atliteg.org/opera/anonimo-mediano/86) calls a
product *prima colatura* only after cloth straining, separate collection and
reservation. V66 reserves *Auszug/Holzauszug* for independently supported
product contexts instead of allowing the R head itself to assert that
workflow.

Likewise K/T continue to be hot/cold quality tags. [Tadhg Ó Cuinn's 1415
*Materia medica*](https://celt.ucc.ie/published/G600006.html) describes
wormwood as hot in the first and dry in the second degree, then gives boiling
and straining as separate operations. V66 therefore adds no heating, cooling
or extraction verb from a nominal R form.
